questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: New Culture, and the ability to see nature which I would never see otherwise

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university itself, was quite dissapointing, the proffessors were mostly non-native english speakers with very strong accents making them difficult to understand.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium, I had to actively search and ask around for all necessary information, but it all went smoothly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any aassistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was quite expensive, but the location was relatively central and accessible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very intuitive and straight forward, however I was quite annoyed when i was denied acces to units due to a lack of units i had yet to complete. I dont understand how it makes sense for the host university to deny my access to a unit if my home university deems it an adequite level for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: very kind people on campus and an intuitive website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was semi succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find all the subjects you want before applying for the university and make sure they don't remove them from their curriculum before you attend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very basic and easy to follow

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty bad, the courses didn't intend for you to have a lecture or class where you could ask questions and the amount of questions and past course information available was very poor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Applied Behavioural Economics, International Economics, Fundamentals of Finance, Financial Markets

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fundanmentals of Finance. The course provided relevant insights, and some challeging calculations, but the rest were quite lacking and/or the professor was terrible at lecturing, due to language issues, a lack of preperation or other issues.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: personally i didn't encounter any unexpected costs, most of my expenses went to travelling throughout the semester visiting most of the east coast of Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: public transport was free, and food were slightly cheaper compared to copenhagen and the rest was pretty much the same

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much anything you would want to do was available to you.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The climbing club was very fun, as well as the exchange trips arranged by the uni clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go north or south on the east coast, there are plenty of amazing beaches and other sights to see which is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, due to it being primarily a western culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate actively in student activities!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the local people, and their eagerness to talk to you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring extra money for travelling, be open to meet new people it will make it so much more fun. Lastly embrace the difficulties, they are a part of the exchange, but they make the fun moments so much better.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students and travelling with them

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: creating an active schedule which contained something exciting to do most days.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
